text: When the Inspector examined the ground a hundred yards round the hollow
why: ¶108: the Inspector says he examined the ground 'very carefully for a hundred yards in each direction.'

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow?
why: The horse has vanished (¶37) and the tracks have just come up empty (¶108), so the question is a plain one the story invites.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — tracks lie beyond the ground searched, or the search missed them
id: q.horse_tracks=tracks lie beyond the ground searched, or the search missed them
why: The Inspector has just reported no more tracks, and Holmes is still searching the ferns, so the tracks lying outside the searched area or being missed is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — led away over ground that takes no prints
id: q.horse_tracks=led away over ground that takes no prints
why: The story describes a moor of ferns, bushes and mud, and the Inspector found no prints, so ground that takes no prints is a reasonable possibility.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — towards Mapleton
why: ¶66 and ¶58-66 establish the Mapleton stables, Silas Brown, and his interest in the race, so Mapleton is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: Which way did the horse go from the hollow? — back towards King's Pyland
why: The horse was taken from the King's Pyland stables (¶28-37), so a return there is a reasonable possibility to consider.
